name: H3_PATCH1_DEV_A
ruling_2026-09-15_ninth: H2_PATCH1 tells us something extremely strong: once the beam actually visits a missing gold node, the node-level patch converts it essentially perfectly. So for deeper hops the bottleneck is now beam recall, not partition selection. We don't need a heavyweight L3. Take the exact frozen real-edge beam and implement each step as batched sparse operations: B_0 = L1 seed nodes; C_{t+1} = N(B_t); B_{t+1} = TopK(frozen score(q, B_t, C_{t+1})) ... scientifically I would continue calling it uL3 ... An H3 arm could simply do: L1 seeds -> H1 beam -> H2 beam -> H3 beam -> novel visited nodes -> same one-block PATCH. No new learned model, no new embeddings, no dataset logic ... For immediate recall improvement: extend the already-successful real-edge beam to a frozen vectorized H3 while keeping PATCH1 at exactly one block-equivalent. That directly targets the hop-3 residual.
why_posthoc: DEV_A has been read by sections 2-16; H2_PATCH1 (section 16) was confirmed on it. This is a mechanism test of ONE further depth step under the identical rule, not a transfer test; transfer needs an untouched population (ruling: WebQSP), DEV_B is not read.

gold_free_input_statistic_read_before_th.decision_taken_from_it: ORDER = the frozen first-visit order (hop-1 beam, hop-2 beam, hop-3 beam), i.e. the H2_PATCH1 rule with DEPTH 2 -> 3 as the ONLY changed factor. Reason (gold-free): under this order the depth-2 patch content is preserved almost exactly (hop-2 novel nodes cut per query: metaqa 0.78, metaqa_phg 0.63, squad 0.01, squad_phg 0.00, musique 0.06) and the positions that H2_PATCH1 filled from the removed block (21.7 / 23.8 / 79.0 / 79.0 / 57.7 per query) are the ones that receive hop-3 nodes (20.9 / 22.9 / 24.9 / 26.1 / 37.3 admitted). The deepest-first order would cut 39.5 / 32.0 hop-2 novel nodes per query on the metaqa caches in 96 % of the queries, i.e. it would dismantle the confirmed section-16 mechanism to make room for hop-3 material; it is NOT run. Consequence stated in advance: on metaqa the one-block budget admits only ~21 of ~68 novel hop-3 visits per query (47 cut; 88 / 49 queries admit none although some exist), so the hop-3 effect is bounded by the budget, not by beam recall; truncation is expected to be the dominant 'available but not covered' reason at depth 3.

population: DEV_A of the five caches metaqa (MtK), metaqa_phg, squad (MtK), squad_phg, musique (PHG); DEV_B not read; TEST never read
metric: ALL-gold at the node level under matched exposure (every gold node served); ANY-gold reported; McNemar exact two-sided

decision_rule.text_safety: on squad, squad_phg and musique: H3_PATCH1 vs H2_PATCH1 AND H3_PATCH1 vs SAFE -- NOT (lost > gained with p < 0.05)
decision_rule.hop3_gain: on BOTH metaqa caches, hop-3 group: H3_PATCH1 vs H2_PATCH1 gained > lost with p < 0.01
decision_rule.no_hop2_regression: on both metaqa caches, hop-2 group: H3_PATCH1 vs H2_PATCH1 -- NOT (lost > gained with p < 0.05)
decision_rule.PASS: all three hold -> H3_PATCH1 = MECHANISM_CONFIRMED_ON_DEV_A (POSTHOC); not promoted; transfer still needs an untouched population
decision_rule.FAIL: otherwise; the reported cause distinguishes (i) budget truncation (hop-3 gold visited but beyond the patch capacity), (ii) beam recall (hop-3 gold not visited at depth 3), (iii) text loss (gold nodes previously restored by the fill dropped)
